original_question: For the quadratic polynomial P_c(z) = z^2 + c, is the Julia set locally connected when c is the Feigenbaum point?
target_in_paper: §1, Question 10, in the paper’s cluster of questions about local connectivity for the quadratic family P_c(z)=z^2+c. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s exact target very closely: it uses the same quadratic family P_c(z)=z^2+c, asks about the same property (local connectivity of the Julia set), and singles out the same parameter choice (the Feigenbaum point). In the paper this is the immediate specialization after the broader Question 8 (“for which c?”) and the real-parameter specialization Question 9. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the ambient setting should be stated explicitly: P_c is a complex quadratic polynomial P_c: C → C, z ↦ z^2+c, and J(P_c) denotes its Julia set. The paper introduces the notation in exactly this quadratic-family context. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The local context in §1 assumes c ranges over parameters for which J(P_c) is connected; that standing restriction is part of the setup immediately before Questions 8–13. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The phrase “the Feigenbaum point” is not defined in the paper right there, so a stand-alone rewrite should identify it explicitly as the real Feigenbaum parameter c_Feig of the quadratic family, i.e. the accumulation point of the real period-doubling cascade. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

It helps to specify that the question concerns local connectivity of the Julia set itself as a subset of C, not the neighboring but different Question 11 about local connectivity of the quadratic connectedness locus (the Mandelbrot set). ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
refined_question: Let P_c: C → C be the quadratic polynomial P_c(z)=z^2+c, and let c=c_Feig denote the real Feigenbaum parameter of the quadratic family (the accumulation point of the period-doubling cascade, so that J(P_c) is connected). Is the Julia set J(P_{c_Feig}) locally connected as a subset of C? ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Question 10 in §1. The paper first fixes the quadratic family by saying “Let P_c(z)=z^2+c where c ranges over values for which the Julia set of P_c is connected,” then asks the broad Question 8 about which such parameters have locally connected Julia sets, the narrower Question 9 for real c, and then the still narrower Question 10 for the Feigenbaum point. So your draft is already essentially paper-faithful; the only real improvements are to make the complex setting and the meaning of “Feigenbaum point” explicit, while avoiding drift to the separate Mandelbrot-set question in Question 11. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
